session_summary: Large documentation-oriented change set with supporting core rewrite work and new tests. The repo gained extensive internal docs around geospatial raster design, batching/state-model plans, product staging, MVP specs, and draft privacy/terms materials. In code, the georesolution pipeline was refactored toward tile batching and async-style staged processing, with new test coverage around batching and request identity. Privacy-related docs now state a stricter MVP direction: no persisted location data, no persisted sent messages, no cookies, and stored registration acknowledgements/block relationships.
human_actions: Review the new geospatial design docs against the current code and assets, especially where documents describe projected rasters, batching ownership, or future pipeline stages rather than already-shipped behavior.
Review `docs/geodata-raster-pipeline-technical.md` for local machine path references (`C:\Users\...`) and replace or clearly label them as local-only notes before wider circulation.

Confirm whether the new privacy-direction docs match actual implementation rather than intended MVP policy, especially for account fields, acknowledgement storage, block persistence, cookies, message persistence, and any location/log retention.
Review the new `spec/mvp/*` feature and interaction files for consistency with current product scope and terminology.
Check whether existing architecture docs such as `architecture-rustles-core.md` now need a refresh to reflect the rewritten `ResolutionQue` structure and new test projects.
Decide whether the new `docs/devlog/...` entry is ready for publication now that its frontmatter changed from `draft: true` to `draft: false`.
Verify solution/test-project changes (`core`, `rustles.core.tests`, `rustles.sln`) are intentional and not duplicate or placeholder test scaffolding.

privacy_summary: Privacy review is required. This diff adds or revises multiple privacy-facing and operational-policy documents asserting that the MVP will store account data, username, age/privacy acknowledgements, and block relationships, while not persisting location data, sent messages, or cookies. The diff also adds MVP specs around authentication, blocking, privacy notice, and municipality chat. These appear to be documentation and product-direction changes more than clearly implemented data-handling changes, so they should be treated as review-required assumptions until verified against code and hosting behavior.
